ecosystem_hall_of_fame.name: Leonardo de Moura & Sebastian Ullrich
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.contribution: Created Lean 4, its kernel, elaborator and module system.
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.bio: Co-founders of the Lean Focused Research Organization (Lean FRO) and chief architects of the Lean 4 theorem prover and programming language, on which Mathlib and both RH/GRH formalizations are built.

ecosystem_hall_of_fame.name: Mathlib maintainers & the Mathlib Initiative
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.contribution: Maintain the mathematical library that defines `riemannZeta`, `RiemannHypothesis`, Dirichlet characters and L-functions.
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.bio: Mathlib is the unified mathematical library whose definitions of `riemannZeta`, `RiemannHypothesis`, Dirichlet characters, and L-functions the formal statements are written against. Its prebuilt cache is the first thing `lake exe cache get` fetches in the RH repository.

ecosystem_hall_of_fame.name: Mario Carneiro
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.contribution: Author of `lean4lean`, an independent Lean 4 kernel written in Lean and one of the external checkers run on the proofs.
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.bio: Author of `lean4lean`, a Lean 4 kernel implemented in Lean. `lean4lean` is one of the checkers that `lake comparator --paranoid` runs, and its results are reported on Andrew Sutherland's verification pages for both proofs.

ecosystem_hall_of_fame.name: Kevin Buzzard & Xena Project
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.contribution: Founder of the Xena Project; leads the formalization of Fermat's Last Theorem in Lean.
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.bio: Professor of Pure Mathematics at Imperial College London and founder of the Xena Project; leads the ongoing formalization of Fermat's Last Theorem in Lean (ImperialCollegeLondon/FLT).

ecosystem_hall_of_fame.name: Sébastien Gouëzel
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.contribution: Mathlib maintainer; noted on Lean Zulip (2026-11-22) that Lean 4.37.0-rc1 gave Mathlib a 23% build speedup, the day before #185 moved RH to 4.37.0-rc1.
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.bio: Mathlib maintainer working on analysis and measure theory. Noted on Lean Zulip on 2026-11-22 that bumping to Lean 4.37.0-rc1 gave Mathlib a 23% build speedup; PR #185 moved RH to 4.37.0-rc1 the next day.

ecosystem_hall_of_fame.name: Andrew Sutherland, Szymon Teżewski & External Checkers
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.org: MIT · Lean kernel / nanoda / lean4lean / con-leche / con-ron
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.contribution: Independent build and export checks of both proofs: the original 61.57 GB export (every module replayed through the Lean kernel; full export accepted by nanoda and con-leche; lean4lean per module; `pp.all` Robin/Lagarias statements) and the shorter grh-lean proof (4.49 GB readable export).
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.bio: Andrew Sutherland (MIT) independently built the original release and reproduced its 61.57 GB export byte for byte: every module replays through the Lean kernel, nanoda and con-leche accept the full export, lean4lean accepts every module, and the `--compare` modes of con-leche and con-ron confirm the five theorems. `pp.all` statement dumps and the Robin/Lagarias statements are published at `math.mit.edu/~drew/grh/`. The shorter proof (lsernau/grh-lean@72fead10) is checked at `math.mit.edu/~drew/shortgrh/`. Szymon Teżewski reported further independent kernels (con-agua, Gruszka, Pestka) on Lean Zulip.

ecosystem_hall_of_fame.name: Johan Commelin & the Lean community
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.contribution: The Lean community statement on the proof is published on the leanprover-community blog; Johan Commelin announced it on Lean Zulip (2026-11-21).
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.bio: The Lean community's statement about the formal proof is published on the leanprover-community blog. Johan Commelin announced it on Lean Zulip on 2026-11-21.

ecosystem_hall_of_fame.name: David Loeffler
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.contribution: Mathlib number-theory contributor; reviewed the original proof's use of unproved literature statements on Lean Zulip (rh#318).
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.bio: Number theorist and Mathlib contributor (zeta and Dirichlet L-function definitions). On Lean Zulip, examined the original proof's `GlobalTheory.Published` literature statements, including ones that are stated but never instantiated (rh#318).

ecosystem_hall_of_fame.name: Levent Alpöge, Christian Merten & Hang Lu Su
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.contribution: Released the formal RH/GRH proof artifact, mapped it via `riemann-blueprint`, and preserved the original release with a prebuilt cache (`riemann-hypothesis-original`).
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.bio: Levent Alpöge released the Lean proof artifact (announced 2026-11-20). Christian Merten built `riemann-blueprint` (chrisflav/riemann-blueprint) to map its structure, and Hang Lu Su (`@homeowmorphism`) maintains the frozen original mirror with a prebuilt community cache.

community_timeline.title: Upstream main switches to the readable edition of lsernau/grh-lean (803 files · ~300k code L)
community_timeline.detail: Kim Morrison moved the 58,947-file community cleanup of the Alpöge proof (Batch 23, 756a70250) to branch alpoge and based main on the readable edition (grh/) of lsernau/grh-lean@72fead10, Luke Sernau's shorter Apache-2.0 version of Levent Alpöge's proof (made with Anthropic colleagues and Claude). Main later moved to Lean v4.37.0-rc1 and added TauCeti as a dependency. Andrew Sutherland (MIT) checked grh-lean@72fead10 on Lean v4.35.0: lake comparator --paranoid accepts (Lean kernel, nanoda, lean4lean, con-leche, con-ron), all 803 modules replay through the kernel, and the 4,485,867,644-byte export is byte-identical on two machines.
